title: Two and a half per cent
word: Two and a half per cent

cards: Forty dates in a bowl, counted out by hand onto a plate. Thirty-nine go back to be eaten, shared, saved. One, just one, is set apart on the edge of the plate.
That's the whole share. When people first hear zakat described as a pillar of the faith, a duty beside the prayer, some expect it to be heavy. A tenth, a quarter, half.
Then comes the number, and it's small. Small enough to keep doing, every year, for a whole life. One coin out of forty: two and a half percent.

teach.b: First, the words. In Sahih al-Bukhari there's a letter Abu Bakr wrote setting out the rules of zakat, and for silver it gives the share as rub' al-'ushr. A quarter of a tenth.
Take a tenth, then a quarter of that, and you have one fortieth: two and a half percent. Second, the same share in coins.

A report in the Sunan of Abu Dawud has the Prophet ﷺ say to bring a quarter of a tenth, one dirham from every forty. And the threshold you met yesterday says it the same way: on two hundred dirhams, five.
Two hundred divided by forty is five. The numbers in these reports agree with each other. Third, what it's charged on.
Not on income as it flows in, and not on everything you own.

teach.h: ON SAVED WEALTH ABOVE THE LINE.
teach.b: On saved wealth above the line, held a year: cash, savings, gold and silver, goods for trade.

Teachers of the law don't count your home, the clothes you wear, or the car you drive to work in the same way, and a later day looks at the categories one by one. Fourth, why such a small share might be the point.
It's something a person can give every year without being ruined by it, and the people who receive it can count on it coming, year after year.
Which is harder than it sounds. Anyone can be generous once.

how: Muslims who owe zakat on money and savings give one fortieth, two and a half percent, of what they hold above the nisab, once a year, some using a mosque's or charity's zakat calculator.

games.q: what does “two and a half per cent” mean?
o: a tenth of every paycheck, given each time it comes in
one fortieth of saved wealth above the line, given yearly
a quarter of all savings, given once in a lifetime

games.q: two and a half percent — tap the pairs.
p: sets out the rules of zakat

s: zakat on savings is a tenth of everything you own
on money it's a quarter of a tenth, one fortieth, and only on saved wealth above the line.
one dirham from every forty and five from two hundred are the same share
two hundred divided by forty is five: the reports agree.
the home you live in is counted for zakat like cash savings
it's charged on saved wealth like cash, gold and trade goods, not on the home you live in.

games.q: you have forty silver dirhams above the threshold, held a full year. how much does the report in Abu Dawud say to bring?
games.why: one dirham from every forty: a quarter of a tenth.

practice: Take a round figure, your savings or any number you'd rather think about, and divide it by ten, then by four: a quarter of a tenth. Hold that number for a breath and notice how big or small it feels next to the whole.
Then breathe out, and picture the thirty-nine parts that stay.

wordCard.voice: Two and a half percent. Rub' al-'ushr, a quarter of a tenth: one fortieth of saved wealth above the threshold. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a quarter of a tenth, the hadith's way of saying one fortieth.

carryVoice: Your line: one in forty. Small enough to keep giving, every single year. Tomorrow: the year, and how long wealth has to sit.
